processing: Fixed, rolled, shaped and dried with no oxidation; production also follows a local technical standard.
harvest_season: Spring. As with other Zhejiang greens, early picking is the prized part.
appearance_dry: Tight, fine strips of lustrous green; the name points to silver down.
taste_profile: Known for a high, lasting aroma and a strong, brisk taste.

brewing.notes: Typical for a curled Zhejiang green: water off the boil, and long steeps turn it sharp.

vintage_note: Sold as the current-year spring green, as is usual for its class, and best within the year. The name also covers a series of related products, so check the harvest date and the origin on the pack.
description:
Songyang Yinhou, silver monkey, is the flagship green tea of Songyang county in Lishui, southwest Zhejiang. It is said to come from the Xie Hou Shan area of the county, and related teas are sold under the same Yinhou name.

The tea is fixed, rolled, shaped and dried, and a local technical standard covers its production.

Local promotion sums up Songyang tea as green colour, tight strips, high aroma and strong flavour. Brew it a bit warmer than a pure bud tea, but watch the time.

The name is promoted widely, so tight, even strips and a clear date are what to check.

Do not mix it up with Bai Mao Hou from Fujian, or with other teas that have monkey in the name, which are quite different.
history:
Tea growing in Songyang is said to go back to the Three Kingdoms, with tribute status claimed for the Tang; those claims are local. Better grounded is the first-class award reported for Songyang tea at the 1929 West Lake Exposition, which went to the county's tea and not to this particular product.

Yinhou itself is modern. One account has the county agriculture bureau developing it in the early 1980s from traditional local methods, with recognition as a Zhejiang famous brand in 2003 and a place among the province's top ten famous teas in 2004. Another links it to a Tang legend of immortal tea attributed to the Taoist Ye Fashan, which is legend.
